summary: The domain is split along the data pipeline of the geosciences: capture (surveying, photogrammetry and lidar, remote sensing), management and analysis (GIS, cartography), the subsurface (geophysics and geological modeling, reservoirs, mines), natural fluids (surface water, groundwater, atmosphere, contaminated sites), and living resources (agriculture; forests, range, wildlife and fire). The geospatial half follows the UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge knowledge areas, the ASPRS divisions and the FIG commissions; the subsurface half follows the SPE technical disciplines and Energistics standards; the natural-system half follows the WMO programmes and the USGS, EPA and USACE model families that O*NET products are mostly built on.

capabilities.name: Geographic information systems
capabilities.definition: Given vector and raster geodata with attributes, store, query, transform and combine them to produce derived layers and answers to spatial questions.
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Geographic information systems and spatial analysis'. Terrain analysis and geostatistics are kept here as tasks rather than as separate capabilities because the same GIS products carry them; routing on street networks is handed to move.

tasks.name: Geodata storage and translation
tasks.definition: Given geodata in mixed formats and coordinate systems, validate, reproject and load it into a managed spatial store or another format without losing geometry or attributes.
tasks.inputs: vector and raster files or services, coordinate reference systems, schema mappings
tasks.outputs: spatial database tables or files in the target format and projection; validation reports
onet_products: Unidata Network common data form NetCDF
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: round-trip fidelity and OGC conformance tests are scoreable; schema mapping is case-specific

tasks.name: Vector overlay and geoprocessing
tasks.definition: Given point, line and polygon layers, compute buffers, clips, intersections, unions, dissolves and spatial joins.
tasks.inputs: vector layers with attributes, tolerances, operation parameters
tasks.outputs: derived vector layers with combined attributes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: results are exact geometry, and robustness suites such as the JTS/GEOS test cases exist

tasks.name: Raster and terrain analysis
tasks.definition: Given elevation and other raster layers, compute map-algebra results and terrain derivatives such as slope, aspect, viewshed, cost distance, flow direction and catchments.
tasks.inputs: digital elevation models and raster layers, analysis parameters
tasks.outputs: derived rasters, viewsheds, least-cost paths, drainage networks and basins

crosswalk.label: Analytics and Modeling (surface and terrain analysis)

onet_products: Geographic resources analysis support system GRASS
ITC Integrated Land and Water Information System ILWIS
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: derivatives on synthetic surfaces have analytic answers and drainage extraction can be scored against mapped streams

tasks.name: Spatial interpolation and geostatistics
tasks.definition: Given measurements at scattered locations, model spatial dependence and predict values and uncertainty on a grid, or test for clustering and hot spots.
tasks.inputs: point samples with values, optional covariates and boundaries
tasks.outputs: variograms, interpolated grids, prediction variance, conditional simulations, cluster statistics
onet_products: Variogram Estimation and Spatial Prediction plus Error Vesper
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: held-out cross-validation error, as in the Spatial Interpolation Comparison exercises
tasks.notes: General statistics lives in science; this node is kept for methods that model spatial dependence.

tasks.name: Land suitability and site selection
tasks.definition: Given criteria layers, weights and constraints, rank locations or allocate land uses and compare planning scenarios.
tasks.inputs: criteria rasters or polygons, weights, constraints, demand targets
tasks.outputs: suitability surfaces, selected sites or corridors, scenario indicators
onet_products: Spatial decision support systems SDSS software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: reserve-selection objectives are scoreable on shared problem sets; criteria weights are a value judgment

tasks.name: Mobile field data capture
tasks.definition: Given a data schema and a GNSS-enabled device, record attributed features and observations in the field and synchronize them with a spatial database.
tasks.inputs: form schemas, basemaps, device positions
tasks.outputs: georeferenced feature records and photos synchronized to a geodatabase
tasks.benchmarkable: no: a workflow tool whose quality is usability and sync reliability

tasks.name: Geocoding and address matching
tasks.definition: Given postal addresses or place names, return coordinates with match quality, and the reverse.
tasks.inputs: address strings, reference street and address-point data
tasks.outputs: coordinates, match scores, standardized addresses
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: match rate and positional error against authoritative address points

tasks.name: Web map and feature services
tasks.definition: Given spatial layers, publish them as standard map, tile, feature and processing services that remote clients can query.
tasks.inputs: spatial layers, styles, service configuration
tasks.outputs: map images, tiles, feature responses and processing results over standard protocols

crosswalk.label: Web Map Service, Web Feature Service, OGC API Features
Geographic human interaction and model/information management services

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: OGC conformance suites test correctness; performance depends on deployment
tasks.notes: General web application platforms belong to computing.

capabilities.name: Cartography and map production
capabilities.definition: Given geodata and a purpose and scale, design and render maps, charts and 3D views that communicate it correctly.

crosswalk.label: Map Design; Generalisation and Multiple Representation; Map Projections

capabilities.notes: Seed kept. Nautical chart compilation is placed here, beside topographic compilation, rather than in surveying, because it is a portrayal and product-specification task.

tasks.name: Thematic map design
tasks.definition: Given attribute data joined to geography, classify and symbolize it as choropleth, proportional-symbol, dot or flow maps with legends and layout.
tasks.inputs: attribute data, boundaries, classification and symbol choices
tasks.outputs: symbolized map layouts and legends
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: rule checks (class breaks, color legibility) are scoreable; overall design quality needs human judgment

tasks.name: Automated label placement
tasks.definition: Given features, label text and placement rules, place labels without overlap and in preferred positions.
tasks.inputs: features, label strings, fonts, priorities and rules
tasks.outputs: label positions and a list of unplaced labels
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: labels placed, conflicts and rule violations are countable on shared datasets

tasks.name: Map projection design
tasks.definition: Given a region and a map purpose, choose and parameterize a projection and report its area, shape and distance distortion.
tasks.inputs: geographic extent, purpose, candidate projections
tasks.outputs: projection definition, distortion statistics, reprojected graticules
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: distortion measures are computable exactly

tasks.name: Map generalization
tasks.definition: Given detailed geodata and a target scale, simplify, aggregate, displace and select features so the map stays legible.
tasks.inputs: large-scale vector data, target scale, constraints
tasks.outputs: generalized vector data
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: constraint violations are measurable; agreement with human-generalized maps is subjective
tasks.notes: No O*NET product names this function directly.

tasks.name: Topographic and thematic base mapping
tasks.definition: Given surveys, imagery and elevation data, compile standard map sheets with contours, hillshade, geology or soil units and standard symbology.
tasks.inputs: survey data, orthoimagery, elevation models, thematic field maps, product specification
tasks.outputs: map sheets and base-map databases
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: completeness and positional accuracy against specification are checkable; symbol design is not

tasks.name: 3D terrain and globe visualization
tasks.definition: Given elevation models, imagery and features, render interactive 3D scenes, virtual globes and fly-throughs.
tasks.inputs: elevation models, imagery, vector features, camera paths
tasks.outputs: interactive 3D scenes, rendered views and animations
tasks.benchmarkable: no: visual quality and interactivity have no reference answer
tasks.notes: General 3D rendering belongs to media.

tasks.name: Nautical chart compilation
tasks.definition: Given validated bathymetry and maritime features, compile electronic and paper navigational charts to the hydrographic product specification.
tasks.inputs: bathymetric surfaces, soundings, aids to navigation, coastline, product specification
tasks.outputs: electronic navigational chart cells and paper charts, validation reports

crosswalk.label: Transfer standard for digital hydrographic data (and S-100 successor)

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: product validation checks (S-58) are scoreable; generalization of soundings needs review
tasks.notes: Chart display and voyage planning aboard ship belong to move.

capabilities.name: Land and hydrographic surveying
capabilities.definition: Given field measurements of angles, distances, satellite signals or sonar returns, compute positions, boundaries and surfaces of land and seafloor with stated accuracy.
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Land surveying, coordinate geometry and GNSS processing'. Hydrographic surveying is added here (FIG treats hydrography as a surveying commission) instead of as its own capability. Civil site, road and corridor design stays in design.

tasks.name: Survey field data collection
tasks.definition: Given an instrument connection and a job file, record coded total-station and GNSS observations and stake out design points.
tasks.inputs: instrument observations, control points, point codes, stakeout coordinates
tasks.outputs: raw observation files, coded points, stakeout reports
tasks.benchmarkable: no: an instrument-control and logging workflow

tasks.name: GNSS post-processing
tasks.definition: Given raw satellite-positioning observations and reference data, compute corrected positions by baseline, differential, kinematic or precise-point processing.
tasks.inputs: raw GNSS observations, base-station or network data, orbits and clocks
tasks.outputs: baseline vectors, corrected coordinates and their precision
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: position error against known stations such as IGS and CORS sites

tasks.name: Least-squares network adjustment
tasks.definition: Given redundant angle, distance, height and GNSS-vector observations and control, compute adjusted coordinates, error ellipses and blunder tests.
tasks.inputs: observations with standard errors, control coordinates
tasks.outputs: adjusted coordinates, residuals, error ellipses, statistical test results
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: published test networks have reference adjusted solutions

tasks.name: Coordinate geometry and boundaries
tasks.definition: Given bearings, distances, curves and legal descriptions, compute coordinates, misclosure, areas and parcel plats.
tasks.inputs: traverse or deed calls, curve data, control points
tasks.outputs: parcel coordinates, closure reports, areas, plat drawings
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: closure and area from a set of calls are exactly computable

tasks.name: Geodetic datum transformation
tasks.definition: Given coordinates in one horizontal or vertical reference frame and projection, convert them to another and report transformation uncertainty.
tasks.inputs: coordinates, source and target reference frames, epochs, geoid and grid models
tasks.outputs: transformed coordinates and heights with uncertainty
onet_products: National Geodetic Survey NGS Geodetic Toolkit
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: agency test points give reference results

tasks.name: Survey drafting and existing surface
tasks.definition: Given coded survey points, build linework, a triangulated existing-ground surface, contours and the survey drawing.
tasks.inputs: coded points, breaklines, drafting standards
tasks.outputs: survey linework, surface model, contours, survey plans
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: the surface and contours from given points are deterministic; linework from codes follows local conventions
tasks.notes: Design surfaces and corridors belong to design.civil_site.

tasks.name: Hydrographic survey and bathymetry processing
tasks.definition: Given planned lines and vessel sensor records (positioning, motion, sound velocity, echo sounder or multibeam), produce cleaned soundings and depth surfaces that meet a survey order.
tasks.inputs: survey lines, raw sonar, positioning, motion and sound-velocity records, tides
tasks.outputs: cleaned soundings, bathymetric grids, uncertainty surfaces, survey reports
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: reference surfaces and IHO total vertical uncertainty limits make results scoreable

tasks.name: Side-scan mosaicking and seabed classification
tasks.definition: Given side-scan or backscatter records, build georeferenced mosaics, pick targets and classify seabed type.
tasks.inputs: side-scan or multibeam backscatter, navigation, ground-truth samples
tasks.outputs: mosaics, target lists, seabed class maps
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: labeled seabed and target datasets exist but are few

capabilities.name: Remote sensing image analysis
capabilities.definition: Given satellite or airborne imagery from optical, thermal or radar sensors, extract calibrated physical quantities, classes, objects and changes.

crosswalk.label: Geographic processing services - thematic (image processing, classification, change detection)

capabilities.notes: Seed 'Remote sensing, photogrammetry and LiDAR processing; drone mission planning' was split: this node takes spectral and radiometric analysis, earth.photogrammetry takes geometric 3D reconstruction, following the ASPRS division between Remote Sensing Applications and Photogrammetric Applications/Lidar.

tasks.name: Radiometric and atmospheric correction
tasks.definition: Given raw image digital numbers and sensor metadata, compute top-of-atmosphere and surface reflectance or brightness temperature, with cloud and shadow masks.
tasks.inputs: raw imagery, calibration coefficients, atmospheric data, acquisition geometry
tasks.outputs: surface reflectance or temperature images, quality masks
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: atmospheric correction intercomparisons score against ground-measured reflectance

tasks.name: Land cover classification
tasks.definition: Given multispectral imagery and training samples, assign each pixel a land-cover class and assess accuracy.
tasks.inputs: image stacks, training and validation samples, class legend
tasks.outputs: class maps, confusion matrices, area estimates
onet_products: ITT Exelis Visual Information Solutions ENVI
ITC Integrated Land and Water Information System ILWIS
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: labeled datasets such as EuroSAT and BigEarthNet

tasks.name: Object-based feature extraction
tasks.definition: Given high-resolution imagery, segment it and extract objects such as buildings, roads, tree crowns or water bodies.
tasks.inputs: high-resolution imagery, optional elevation and training labels, rule sets
tasks.outputs: object polygons or lines with class and attributes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SpaceNet building and road challenges

tasks.name: Change detection and image time series
tasks.definition: Given co-registered images over time, map where and when the surface changed and characterize trends and seasonal cycles.
tasks.inputs: multi-date image stacks, masks, change legend
tasks.outputs: change maps, disturbance dates, trend and phenology metrics
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: labeled change datasets such as OSCD and xView2

tasks.name: Hyperspectral and spectral analysis
tasks.definition: Given spectral image cubes and spectral libraries, identify materials and estimate their abundance per pixel.
tasks.inputs: hyperspectral or multispectral cubes, spectral libraries
tasks.outputs: material and abundance maps, anomaly and target detections
onet_products: ITT Exelis Visual Information Solutions ENVI
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: standard scenes (Indian Pines, Pavia) have ground truth but are small

tasks.name: Radar imaging and interferometry
tasks.definition: Given synthetic-aperture radar acquisitions, produce calibrated backscatter, coherence, interferograms and surface-deformation time series.
tasks.inputs: SAR single-look complex or detected images, orbits, elevation model
tasks.outputs: backscatter images, interferograms, displacement maps and time series
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: deformation estimates can be scored against GNSS stations

tasks.name: Image interpretation and mensuration
tasks.definition: Given georeferenced imagery, let an analyst view, measure, annotate and report on features and activity.
tasks.inputs: imagery with sensor models, reference data
tasks.outputs: measurements, annotated products, reports
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: mensuration accuracy is scoreable; interpretation is analyst judgment

capabilities.name: Photogrammetry, lidar and aerial mapping
capabilities.definition: Given overlapping images or laser scans from aircraft, drones or ground vehicles, reconstruct accurate 3D geometry: orientations, point clouds, elevation models and orthoimages.

crosswalk.label: LAS point cloud format; Positional Accuracy Standards for Digital Geospatial Data

capabilities.notes: Split from the remote-sensing seed (see earth.remote_sensing). Drone mission planning is kept as a mapping task (coverage, overlap, ground sample distance); flying and airspace operations belong to move.

tasks.name: Aerial mapping mission planning
tasks.definition: Given an area, a sensor and an accuracy target, compute flight lines, altitude, overlap and waypoints that achieve the required coverage and ground sample distance.
tasks.inputs: area of interest, camera or lidar specification, terrain, accuracy and overlap requirements
tasks.outputs: flight plan, waypoints, predicted coverage and resolution
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: coverage and resolution are computable; feasibility depends on airspace and aircraft

tasks.name: Aerial triangulation and bundle adjustment
tasks.definition: Given overlapping images, approximate positions and ground control, solve camera orientations and tie-point coordinates by least-squares bundle adjustment.
tasks.inputs: images, camera calibration, GNSS/IMU data, ground control points
tasks.outputs: exterior and interior orientations, tie points, accuracy report
onet_products: Intergraph ImageStation Stereo Softcopy Kit SSK
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ISPRS and EuroSDR benchmark blocks have independent checkpoints

tasks.name: Structure from motion and dense matching
tasks.definition: Given unordered overlapping photographs, recover camera poses and a dense 3D point cloud or mesh.
tasks.inputs: photographs, optional positions and control
tasks.outputs: camera poses, sparse and dense point clouds, textured meshes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ETH3D and Tanks and Temples score reconstructions against laser-scanned ground truth

tasks.name: Orthorectification and mosaicking
tasks.definition: Given oriented images and an elevation model, remove relief and tilt displacement and blend the images into a seamless orthomosaic.
tasks.inputs: images, orientations or sensor models, elevation model
tasks.outputs: orthoimages, seamlines, mosaics, accuracy report
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: checkpoint error under the ASPRS positional accuracy standard

tasks.name: Stereo feature compilation
tasks.definition: Given oriented stereo pairs, digitize 3D features such as breaklines, buildings, roads and hydrography.
tasks.inputs: oriented stereo models, feature specification
tasks.outputs: 3D vector features
onet_products: Intergraph ImageStation Stereo Softcopy Kit SSK
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: positional accuracy is scoreable against checkpoints; completeness depends on the specification

tasks.name: Lidar point cloud classification
tasks.definition: Given georeferenced lidar or image-derived points, label them as ground, vegetation, buildings, water and other standard classes.
tasks.inputs: point clouds with intensity and returns, trajectories, class scheme
tasks.outputs: classified point clouds, strip-alignment and accuracy reports
onet_products: GeoCue LIDAR and drone mapping software
Laser imaging detection and ranging LIDAR system
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ISPRS filter test, DALES and Semantic3D have labeled points

tasks.name: Elevation model generation
tasks.definition: Given classified points or stereo matches, interpolate bare-earth and surface elevation models with breaklines and contours.
tasks.inputs: classified point clouds or stereo matches, breaklines
tasks.outputs: digital terrain and surface models, contours, vertical accuracy report
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: vertical error against surveyed checkpoints

tasks.name: Mobile mapping and SLAM
tasks.definition: Given lidar, camera and inertial streams from a moving platform, estimate its trajectory and build a consistent georeferenced map.
tasks.inputs: lidar scans, images, IMU and GNSS streams
tasks.outputs: trajectory, registered point cloud or map
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: KITTI odometry and Hilti SLAM challenge score trajectory error

capabilities.name: Subsurface imaging and geological modeling
capabilities.definition: Given seismic, potential-field, electrical and well measurements, image the subsurface and build interpreted 3D geological models.

crosswalk.scheme: SEG (Society of Exploration Geophysicists) technical areas
crosswalk.label: Seismic acquisition and processing; interpretation; near-surface; mining geophysics

onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: Seed 'Subsurface modeling: geology, seismic interpretation, reservoir and mine planning' was split three ways: imaging and geological modeling here, flow and well performance in earth.reservoir, and mine planning in earth.mining, because each has its own inputs, outputs and product families. Soil and rock mechanics for design stay in simulate.

tasks.name: Seismic data processing and imaging
tasks.definition: Given field seismic records and acquisition geometry, apply corrections, velocity analysis, stacking and migration to produce subsurface images.
tasks.inputs: shot records, geometry, velocity models
tasks.outputs: stacked and migrated volumes, velocity models
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic models such as Marmousi and the SEG/EAGE salt model have known truth

tasks.name: Seismic interpretation
tasks.definition: Given migrated seismic volumes and well ties, pick horizons and faults, compute attributes and convert time to depth.
tasks.inputs: seismic volumes, well logs and tops, velocity data
tasks.outputs: horizon and fault surfaces, attribute volumes, time and depth maps
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: labeled fault and facies volumes such as the F3 Netherlands facies benchmark

tasks.name: Seismic inversion and rock physics
tasks.definition: Given seismic data and well logs, estimate elastic properties, run amplitude-versus-offset analysis and relate them to lithology and fluids.
tasks.inputs: pre- or post-stack seismic, wavelets, well logs, rock physics models
tasks.outputs: impedance and elastic property volumes, synthetic seismograms, lithology and fluid probability
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic earth models with known properties allow exact scoring

tasks.name: Potential-field and near-surface geophysics
tasks.definition: Given gravity, magnetic, electrical, electromagnetic or refraction measurements, produce anomaly maps and forward or inverted earth models.
tasks.inputs: survey readings, station positions, terrain, starting models
tasks.outputs: corrected anomaly grids, 2D and 3D property models, depth-to-source estimates
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic models with known structure

tasks.name: Well log analysis and petrophysics
tasks.definition: Given wireline or drilling logs and core data, compute porosity, water saturation, lithology and net pay.
tasks.inputs: log curves, core measurements, formation tops, parameters
tasks.outputs: petrophysical curves, zone summaries, net-pay reports
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: FORCE 2020 lithology and SPWLA prediction contests

tasks.name: Borehole logs and stratigraphic correlation
tasks.definition: Given borehole descriptions, samples and logs, draft log plots and correlate units into cross sections and fence diagrams.
tasks.inputs: lithology descriptions, sample and test results, downhole logs, locations
tasks.outputs: borehole log plots, correlated cross sections, fence diagrams
tasks.benchmarkable: no: drafting and interpretive correlation without a reference answer
tasks.notes: Geotechnical test interpretation for design belongs to simulate.geotechnical.

tasks.name: Structural and 3D geological modeling
tasks.definition: Given horizons, faults, well tops and outcrop data, build a consistent 3D structural framework, restore sections and populate property grids.
tasks.inputs: interpreted surfaces, fault sticks, well tops, orientation data, property data
tasks.outputs: 3D structural models, restored sections, gridded property models
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: synthetic models test reproduction of known structure; interpretation is non-unique

tasks.name: Basin and petroleum system modeling
tasks.definition: Given stratigraphy, lithology and heat-flow history, simulate burial, temperature, maturity and hydrocarbon generation and migration.
tasks.inputs: layer ages and thicknesses, lithologies, heat flow, source-rock kinetics
tasks.outputs: burial and thermal histories, maturity maps, charge and migration estimates
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: calibration to measured temperature and vitrinite reflectance in wells

capabilities.name: Reservoir and well performance engineering
capabilities.definition: Given a reservoir description, fluid properties and well data, predict flow, pressure and recoverable volumes over time.

crosswalk.label: Reservoir Description and Dynamics; Production and Operations

capabilities.notes: Split from the subsurface seed. Pipelines and surface gathering networks are engineered networks (simulate); drilling operations reporting goes to operate.

tasks.name: Reservoir flow simulation
tasks.definition: Given a gridded reservoir model, fluid and rock properties and well controls, simulate multiphase flow and forecast production and pressure.
tasks.inputs: property grids, relative permeability and capillary data, fluid model, well schedules
tasks.outputs: pressure and saturation fields, well rates, forecasts
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SPE Comparative Solution Projects provide shared problems and reference results

tasks.name: Reservoir fluid characterization
tasks.definition: Given laboratory pressure-volume-temperature data, tune an equation-of-state or black-oil model of the reservoir fluid.
tasks.inputs: fluid composition, lab experiments (constant composition expansion, differential liberation, separator tests)
tasks.outputs: tuned equation-of-state model, black-oil tables
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: error against measured lab properties on public fluid datasets
tasks.notes: General thermodynamic property packages belong to simulate's process flowsheeting.

tasks.name: Well inflow and lift performance
tasks.definition: Given reservoir, completion and tubing data, compute inflow and vertical-lift curves, operating rates and artificial-lift designs.
tasks.inputs: reservoir pressure and productivity, completion and tubing geometry, fluid model
tasks.outputs: inflow and outflow curves, operating point, lift design
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: correlations can be scored against measured well tests

tasks.name: Pressure transient analysis
tasks.definition: Given flow-rate and pressure records from a well test, estimate permeability, skin, boundaries and reservoir pressure.
tasks.inputs: rate and pressure history, well and fluid properties
tasks.outputs: diagnostic plots, model match, reservoir parameters
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic tests with known parameters
tasks.notes: Aquifer tests are the groundwater analogue (earth.groundwater.aquifer_tests).

tasks.name: Decline analysis and reserves evaluation
tasks.definition: Given production history and economics, forecast rates, estimate ultimate recovery and classify reserves.
tasks.inputs: monthly production, prices, costs, ownership
tasks.outputs: rate forecasts, estimated ultimate recovery, reserves and cash-flow reports
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: hindcasts on public state production data are scoreable

capabilities.name: Mineral resource and mine planning
capabilities.definition: Given drillhole data, a geological model and economic parameters, estimate the mineral resource and design and schedule its extraction.

crosswalk.label: Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves classification

onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: Split from the subsurface seed. Mine fleet dispatch is vehicle operations (move); rock mechanics and roof support are geotechnical analysis (simulate).

tasks.name: Drillhole data management and compositing
tasks.definition: Given collars, downhole surveys, assays and geology logs, validate them into a drillhole database and produce composites.
tasks.inputs: collar, survey, assay and lithology tables
tasks.outputs: validated drillhole database, 3D traces, composites
tasks.benchmarkable: no: data management without a reference answer

tasks.name: Block modeling and resource estimation
tasks.definition: Given composites and geological domains, estimate grades into a block model and classify the resource by confidence.
tasks.inputs: composites, domain wireframes, variograms, estimation parameters
tasks.outputs: block model with grades and classification, grade-tonnage curves
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic and exhaustive datasets (Walker Lake) allow scoring estimates against truth

tasks.name: Open-pit limit optimization
tasks.definition: Given block economic values and slope constraints, find the ultimate pit and nested shells that maximize value.
tasks.inputs: block model with values, slope angles, prices and costs
tasks.outputs: ultimate pit, nested shells, pushback candidates
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: MineLib instances have known optima
tasks.notes: Gemcom PCBC is the block-cave analogue for underground mines.

tasks.name: Mine layout design
tasks.definition: Given an optimal shell or stope envelope, design practical benches, ramps, stopes and development openings.
tasks.inputs: pit shells or stope shapes, design parameters, topography
tasks.outputs: pit and underground designs, reserve volumes
onet_products: Ohio Automation Integrated Computer Aided Mine Planning System ICAMPS
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: designs can be checked against constraints and shell volume; practicality needs review

tasks.name: Mine production scheduling
tasks.definition: Given a reserve model, precedences and capacities, schedule extraction by period to maximize net present value.
tasks.inputs: mining blocks or solids, precedences, equipment and plant capacities, economics
tasks.outputs: period schedules, stockpile plans, NPV
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: MineLib scheduling instances have best known solutions
tasks.notes: General optimization solvers belong to science.

capabilities.name: Surface water hydrology and hydraulics
capabilities.definition: Given precipitation, terrain, land cover, soils and channel geometry, predict runoff, river flows, water levels, floods, erosion and water quality in natural waters.

crosswalk.scheme: USACE Hydrologic Engineering Center model family
crosswalk.label: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Hydrology and natural water modeling (rivers, watersheds, groundwater, coasts)'; groundwater split into earth.groundwater. Pressurized water, sewer and storm-drain pipe networks belong to simulate; urban runoff generation stays here.

tasks.name: Rainfall-runoff and watershed modeling
tasks.definition: Given precipitation, basin geometry, land cover and soils, compute infiltration, runoff hydrographs and continuous streamflow.
tasks.inputs: rainfall or meteorological series, subbasin parameters, loss and routing methods
tasks.outputs: runoff hydrographs, peak flows, water balances

crosswalk.scheme: USACE Hydrologic Engineering Center model family
crosswalk.label: HEC-HMS

onet_products: Hydrologic simulation program fortan HSPF software
HydroCAD Software Solutions HydroCAD Stormwater Modeling System
EPA Storm Water Management Model SWMM
DHI Water and Environment MIKE SHE
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: CAMELS catchments give observed streamflow for scoring

tasks.name: Open-channel and river hydraulics
tasks.definition: Given channel and floodplain geometry, roughness, structures and flows, compute water-surface profiles, velocities and shear in one or two dimensions.
tasks.inputs: cross sections or terrain mesh, roughness, bridges and culverts, boundary flows
tasks.outputs: water-surface elevations, velocities, depths, hydraulic tables

crosswalk.scheme: USACE Hydrologic Engineering Center model family
crosswalk.label: HEC-RAS

onet_products: Surface water modeling system SMS software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the UK Environment Agency 2D hydraulic benchmark tests
tasks.notes: Culverts and fish passage are kept here because they are natural-channel hydraulics.

tasks.name: Flood inundation and hazard mapping
tasks.definition: Given design or observed flows and terrain, map flood extent, depth and hazard zones.
tasks.inputs: flow frequencies or hydraulic results, terrain models, structures
tasks.outputs: inundation extents, depth grids, flood-zone maps
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: observed flood extents from imagery give a reference

tasks.name: Hydrologic data and frequency analysis
tasks.definition: Given gauge and logger records, quality-control the series, build rating curves and estimate flow and rainfall frequency.
tasks.inputs: stage, discharge and rainfall records, field measurements
tasks.outputs: cleaned series, rating curves, frequency curves and design values
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: published frequency estimates for test sites

tasks.name: Surface water quality and loading
tasks.definition: Given pollutant sources, flows and kinetics, simulate nutrient, sediment and contaminant concentrations in streams and lakes and allocate loads.
tasks.inputs: point and nonpoint loads, flows, reaction rates, temperatures
tasks.outputs: concentration series, load budgets, load allocations
onet_products: Hydrologic simulation program fortan HSPF software
Water Soil and Hydro-Environmental Decision Support System WATERSHEDSS
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: monitored concentrations exist but calibration data are sparse

tasks.name: Soil erosion and sediment yield
tasks.definition: Given rainfall, soils, slopes, cover and practices, estimate soil loss, sediment delivery and pond trapping.
tasks.inputs: rainfall erosivity, soil erodibility, slope, cover and practice factors or process parameters
tasks.outputs: soil loss rates, sediment yields, basin trap efficiency
onet_products: Revised universal soil loss equation RUSLE software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: plot-scale erosion datasets exist

tasks.name: Coastal and estuarine hydrodynamics
tasks.definition: Given bathymetry, tides, winds and river inflows, simulate water levels, currents, waves, storm surge and salinity.
tasks.inputs: bathymetric mesh, tidal and meteorological forcing, river inflows
tasks.outputs: water levels, currents, wave fields, surge and salinity
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: hindcasts scored against tide gauges and wave buoys

open_questions: Capability count is 14, at the top of the range. If the editor wants fewer, the cleanest merges are earth.reservoir into earth.subsurface and earth.environmental_site into earth.groundwater; if more are allowed, livestock (herd records, rations, genetics) should become its own capability apart from crops and soils.
Urban stormwater sits on the boundary: SWMM-type runoff generation is placed here, storm-drain pipe hydraulics in simulate. The editor should confirm simulate uses the same cut.
Geotechnical seepage (SEEP/W) and slope stability were handed to simulate per the boundary table, but hydrologists and conservation scientists are the listed users; confirm simulate takes them.

Many products are public datasets rather than software (SSURGO, STATSGO, NLCD, NARCCAP tables, satellite image databases). I listed some as examples of the task their data serves and left pure data products unplaced; the editor should decide a policy for data products.

A small family of geology calculators (paleomagnetism, strain, petrologic mass balance, stereonets: PaleoMag, StrainSim, Gresens 92, RockPack) has no node. A task 'structural geology and petrologic calculations' could be added under earth.subsurface if a home is wanted.

Several Scientific Software Group product names in the unplaced list could not be identified confidently from the name alone; a later pass with product descriptions could place them, most likely in earth.groundwater or earth.environmental_site.
